summary: An erech is never less than one sela and never more than fifty. The mishnah then lists other things in the Torah that have a smallest and a biggest number.

chunks.en: For an erech, no one pays less than one sela,
chunks.explain: A poor person pays what he can, but at least one sela.
chunks.st: One cannot be charged for a valuation less than a sela,

chunks.en: and no one pays more than fifty sela'im.
chunks.st: nor can one be charged more than fifty sela.

chunks.en: How so? If a poor person gave one sela and later became rich,
chunks.st: How so? If one gave one sela and became wealthy,

chunks.en: he does not have to give anything more.
chunks.st: he is not required to give anything more, as he has fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he gave less than a sela and then became rich,
chunks.st: If he gave less than a sela and became wealthy,

chunks.en: he must give fifty sela'im.
chunks.st: he is required to give fifty sela, as he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If the poor person had five sela'im,
chunks.st: If there were five sela in the possession of the destitute person,
chunks.stMore: and the valuation he undertook is more than five sela, how much should he pay?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he gives only one.
chunks.st: He gives only one sela and thereby fulfills his obligation.

chunks.en: And the Chachamim say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he gives all of them.
chunks.st: He gives all five.

chunks.en: For an erech, no one pays less than one sela,
chunks.st: One cannot be charged for a valuation less than a sela;

chunks.en: and no one pays more than fifty sela'im.
chunks.st: nor can one be charged more than fifty sela.

chunks.en: A woman who is unsure about a kind of tumah cannot become tahor in fewer than seven clean days,
chunks.st: If a woman experienced a discharge of blood and is unsure whether it was during her days of menstruation or during the eleven days that would render her a zava, the alleviation of her state of uncertainty does not occur in fewer than seven clean days,

chunks.en: and it never takes more than seventeen.
chunks.st: nor in more than seventeen clean days,
chunks.stMore: depending on the number of days that she experiences the discharge.

chunks.en: For tzaraas marks, the Kohen never closes a person away for less than one week,
chunks.st: There are symptoms of leprosy that a priest will immediately confirm to be ritually pure or ritually impure, and there are others for which the priest quarantines the leper in order to determine his status. With regard to leprous marks, there is no quarantine that is less than one week

words.note: Tzaraas is a skin sickness from the Torah; a Kohen looks at the marks.

chunks.en: and never more than three weeks.
chunks.st: and none greater than three weeks.

summary: More things that have a smallest and a biggest number: full months in a year, when the Two Loaves and the lechem hapanim are eaten, and the day of a bris milah.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵאַרְבָּעָה חֲדָשִׁים הַמְעֻבָּרִים בְּשָׁנָה,
chunks.en: There are no fewer than four full months in a year,
chunks.explain: A full month has thirty days.
chunks.st: No fewer than four full thirty-day months may be established during the course of a year,

chunks.en: and it did not seem right to have more than eight.
chunks.st: and it did not seem appropriate to establish more than eight.

chunks.en: The Two Loaves of Shavuos are eaten no sooner
chunks.st: The two loaves that are brought to the Temple on Shavuot are eaten by the priests not before

words.note: Two special breads brought in the Beis Hamikdash on Shavuos.

chunks.en: than the second day after baking, and no later than the third.
chunks.st: the second and not after the third day from when they were baked.

chunks.he: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים נֶאֱכָל אֵין פָּחוּת מִתִּשְׁעָה
chunks.en: The lechem hapanim is eaten no sooner than the ninth day after baking,
chunks.st: The shewbread is eaten not before the ninth day from when it was baked,
chunks.stMore: which is the situation in a regular week when the bread is baked on Friday and eaten on the following Shabbat;

words.note: The lechem hapanim, breads that stayed on the golden table all week.

chunks.en: and no later than the eleventh.
chunks.st: and not after the eleventh day,
chunks.stMore: when the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana occur on Thursday and Friday, as the shewbread is baked on Wednesday and not eaten until the following Shabbat.

chunks.en: A baby boy has his bris milah no sooner than the eighth day,
chunks.st: A minor boy is not circumcised before the eighth day after his birth

chunks.en: and no later than the twelfth day.
chunks.st: and not after the twelfth day.
chunks.stMore: Normally a newborn is circumcised on his eighth day. If he was born during twilight, which an uncertain period of day or night, he is circumcised on what would be the eighth day of his birth if he is was born at night, which is the ninth day if he was born during the day. If he was born during twilight on Shabbat eve, the circumcision cannot be performed on Friday, as he might have been born on Shabbat and therefore Friday is only the seventh day. And the circumcision cannot be on Shabbat, as perhaps he was born on Friday and only circumcision performed on the eighth day overrides Shabbat. Therefore, it is postponed until after Shabbat. If two days of Rosh HaShana occur on Sunday and Monday, the circumcision is postponed until Tuesday, the twelfth day after birth.

summary: How many trumpet blasts, harps and flutes were used in the Beis Hamikdash, and on which twelve days the flute was played before the mizbe'ach.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
chunks.en: They blow no fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts each day in the Beis Hamikdash,
chunks.st: No fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts are sounded daily in the Temple,
chunks.stMore: as each day three blasts were sounded for the opening of the gates in the morning, nine for the daily morning offering, and nine for the daily afternoon offering, totaling twenty-one.

chunks.en: and never more than forty-eight.
chunks.st: And no more than forty-eight are ever sounded on a single day.
chunks.stMore: This would occur on the Friday of Sukkot, when they would sound an additional twelve blasts during the ritual of drawing the water for the water libation; nine for the additional offerings; three to signal the population to cease their work before Shabbat; and three more to mark the beginning of Shabbat.

chunks.en: The Levi'im play no fewer than two lyres,
chunks.st: When accompanying their song with instruments, the Levites do not use fewer than two lyres

chunks.en: and no more than six.
chunks.st: and do not use more than six.

chunks.en: They play no fewer than two flutes, and no
chunks.st: When flutes are played, they do not use fewer than two flutes and

chunks.en: more than twelve.
chunks.st: do not use more than twelve.

chunks.en: And on twelve days of the year
chunks.st: And there are twelve days during the year

chunks.en: the flute is played before the mizbe'ach:
chunks.st: when the flute plays before the altar:

chunks.en: when the first Korban Pesach is shechted,
chunks.st: At the time of the slaughter of the first Paschal offering,

chunks.en: when the second Korban Pesach, Pesach Sheni, is shechted,
chunks.st: and at the time of the slaughter of the second Paschal offering,

chunks.en: on the first Yom Tov of Pesach,
chunks.st: and on the first festival day of Passover;

chunks.en: on the Yom Tov of Shavuos,
chunks.st: and on the festival of Shavuot;

chunks.en: and on the eight days of Sukkos.
chunks.st: and on all eight days of the festival of Sukkot.

chunks.en: And they would not play on a flute made of
chunks.st: And one would not play with a

chunks.en: copper, but only on a flute made of reed,
chunks.st: copper flute; rather, one would play with a flute of reed,

chunks.en: because its sound is sweeter.
chunks.st: because its sound is more pleasant.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה מַחֲלִיק אֶלָּא בְאַבּוּב יְחִידִי,
chunks.en: And they would end the music with only one flute,
chunks.st: And one would conclude the music only with a single flute,

chunks.en: because that makes a nice ending.
chunks.st: because it concludes the music nicely.

summary: Who were the people who played music in the Beis Hamikdash? The Tannaim argue.

chunks.en: They were slaves of the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The Temple musicians were slaves of priests;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: they were from the families of Beis Hapegarim and Beis Tzipparya
chunks.st: The musicians were not slaves, but Israelites from the family of the house of Pegarim and the family of the house of Tzippara

chunks.en: from Emaum, and they would marry their daughters to Kohanim.
chunks.st: from the city of Emaum, and their lineage was sufficiently pure that they would marry their daughters to members of the priesthood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: they were Levi'im.
chunks.st: They were Levites.

summary: How many checked lambs were kept ready in the Beis Hamikdash, and how many trumpets, harps and cymbals were played.

chunks.en: They keep no fewer than six lambs
chunks.st: One maintains no fewer than six lambs that

chunks.en: that were checked for blemishes in the Lamb Room,
chunks.st: have been inspected for blemishes in the Chamber of the Lambs,

chunks.en: enough for Shabbos and the two days
chunks.st: which are sufficient for the offerings of Shabbat and for the two

chunks.en: of Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah,
chunks.st: Festival days of Rosh HaShana that may occur adjacent to it.

chunks.en: and they may add as many as they want.
chunks.st: And one may add inspected lambs up to an infinite number.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד לְעוֹלָם.
chunks.en: They play no fewer than two trumpets, and they may add as many as they want.
chunks.st: One plays no fewer than two trumpets

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִתִּשְׁעָה כִנּוֹרוֹת, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד לְעוֹלָם.
chunks.en: They play no fewer than nine harps, and they may add as many as they want.
chunks.st: and no fewer than nine harps in the Temple, and one may add up to an infinite number.

chunks.en: But the cymbal is played alone.
chunks.st: And the cymbal was played alone, and none may be added to it.

summary: How many Levi'im stood on the platform to sing, and how young Levi'im joined the singing.

chunks.en: There are no fewer than twelve
chunks.st: In the Temple, there are no fewer than twelve

chunks.en: Levi'im standing on the platform and singing,
chunks.st: Levites standing on the platform adjacent to the altar and singing,

chunks.en: and they may add as many as they want.
chunks.st: and one may add Levites on the platform up to an infinite number.

chunks.en: A young boy does not come into the Azarah to serve,
chunks.st: A minor Levite may enter the Temple courtyard for service

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis Hamikdash.

chunks.en: except when the Levi'im are standing and singing.
chunks.st: only at a time when the Levites are engaging in song, so that he may accompany them.

chunks.en: And the boys would not play on a lyre
chunks.st: And minors would not engage in playing a lyre

chunks.en: or a harp, only sing with their mouth,
chunks.st: and in playing a harp; rather, they would engage in singing with the mouth,

chunks.en: to give a sweet taste to the music.
chunks.st: in order to provide flavor to the music with their pure, high voices.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: the boys are not counted in the number,
chunks.st: Minors are not tallied in the minimum total of twelve Levites,

chunks.en: and they do not stand on the platform,
chunks.st: and they do not ascend to the platform;

chunks.en: but they would stand on the ground,
chunks.st: rather, they would stand on the ground

chunks.en: and their heads reached between the legs of the Levi'im,
chunks.st: and their heads would reach to between the legs of the Levites,

chunks.en: and they were called the young helpers of the Levi'im.
chunks.st: and they were called cadets [tzoarei] of the Levites.
